differences.what: massing: the light ashlar block two storeys over a raised basement, its wall head at about 10.75 m under a slated mansard with an iron cresting on its curb; the front's north corner at the cornice's bed lands within 4 px of the print's (x 412, y 515)
the porch on paired columns at the stoop's head and its balustraded balcony before the window over the door (x 470-750 px)
the front's north window column and the window over the porch, both storeys, under moulded heads (x 485-545 and 620-700 px)

the two tall stacks on the south flank, laid in the walls' pale stone (the render's had been red brick), one near the front corner (x 1110-1180 px) and one east of the flank's dormer (x 1455-1500 px), both standing on the cornice over the side wall
a pedimented dormer on the south flank's mansard face over the canted bay's west end (x 1380-1450 px); the render had none on that face
the fence: a band of iron scrolls on a stone curb, with tall square stone posts at the gate; now K11's scroll-band fence on the kit's stone piers (the render's had been spear pickets on iron posts)

the front's south-west corner: this photograph cuts it on a canted face square to its camera, about 1.83 m back each way (x 942-1120 px, about 2.6 m across), with its own window column on both storeys, its own pedimented dormer over them, and the cornice and the mansard carried round it; the render's corner is square. K01 cuts a corner only on a shallow pavilion (at most 1.0 m) or rounds it corbelled back to square under the wall head (1811's), so the whole cut through the cornice and the mansard is new K01 geometry, not a parameter

the stoop's cheeks: the print's sweep down and out from the porch's column plinths to a roll at the walk (x 340-500 and 545-700 px); the render's are straight. K01's swept cheek stands only beside a terrace behind a pierced parapet and its scrolled one beside none, and this porch's columns stand on terraces the print shows open
the porch's columns: Corinthian capitals on paired shafts set close; the render's are plain shafts under block capitals, K01's door-hood column, which has no carved capital

the cornice: the print's is deep, on large paired blocks over a frieze about 0.6-0.8 m high, round the front, the canted corner and the flank; the render's K10 moulded cornice is thinner, its blocks single

the dormers' pediments: the print's are low triangular pediments with a level cornice across their foot and carved cheeks, the canted corner's the largest; the render's stand at K01's lowest pitch, 30 deg, without the level cornice or the carving

the south flank's canted bay: its west cheek, which faces this camera, reads about 3 m across in the print (x 1340-1522 px) where the 1911 sheet's bay gives it 2.25 m; the camera's largest residuals (16-22 px) are there. Two plans (the sheet and this fit) disagree, so it is not moved here

the flank's two narrow window columns and the carved cartouche between the canted corner and the bay (x 1200-1330 px); the render's flank windows stand in K01's ordinary widths and there is no cartouche
colour: the print is monochrome; the stone's buff and the slate's grey are the kit's
the rear and the brick rear range, behind the trees

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153). A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
